what_its_for: Etravirine is an antiviral medicine used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children who are at least 2 years old. It belongs to a group of medicines called non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). It helps lower the amount of HIV in your blood and keeps your immune system working better. It is always used together with other HIV medicines — never alone.
how_to_take: Take etravirine by mouth AFTER a meal — do not take it on an empty stomach, as food helps your body absorb the medicine properly. Swallow the tablets whole with water. If you have trouble swallowing tablets, you may dissolve them in a glass of water: add the tablets to at least 5 teaspoons of water, stir well until the water looks milky, and drink it right away. Rinse the glass with more water and drink that too, to make sure you get the full dose.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 200 mg (two 100 mg tablets) taken TWICE daily — once in the morning and once in the evening, always with food. For children, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 6 hours since your scheduled dose time, take the missed dose with food as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. Taking your medicine at the same times every day is very important to keep HIV under control.
storage: Store etravirine at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in the original bottle with the cap tightly closed. Protect it from moisture and heat — do not store it in the bathroom or near a sink. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Do not take certain medicines with etravirine without talking to your doctor first — many drugs can interact with it and make it less effective or cause serious side effects. These include: rifampin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), and some other HIV medicines. Always tell EVERY doctor, dentist, and pharmacist that you take etravirine before starting any new medicine, supplement, or herbal product. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol. Do not stop taking your HIV medicines without your doctor's approval, even if you feel fine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: a skin rash (especially with blistering, peeling, sores in your mouth, or fever — this could be a rare but serious reaction called Stevens-Johnson Syndrome); yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools; severe stomach pain; unusual tiredness or weakness; signs of liver problems; mood changes, depression, or thoughts of self-harm; or any signs of a new infection. Call 911 or go to the emergency room immediately if you have trouble breathing, severe rash covering your whole body, or swelling of your face, lips, or throat.
when_it_works: Etravirine does NOT cure HIV, but it helps control it. It may take several weeks before you see a change in your lab results (viral load and CD4 count). Most people start to see the HIV level in their blood go down within the first few weeks. Keep taking your medicine every day even if you feel well — stopping treatment allows the virus to multiply and can make it harder to treat later. Regular blood tests will help your doctor check how well the medicine is working.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. HIV medicines may be needed during pregnancy to protect both you and your baby, but your doctor will carefully review your treatment plan. BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed if you have HIV, as the virus can pass to your baby through breast milk. KIDNEY or LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how your body processes the medicine. CHILDREN: Etravirine can be used in children 2 years and older who weigh at least 22 pounds (10 kg); the dose is based on your child's weight. OLDER ADULTS: Use with caution in older adults; your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects.
